Butler changed the corrupt ἀτιμίας [dishonor] to ἀτρεμαῖα [unmoved], used adverbially as in Eur. Herc. f. 1054, comparing the scholiast's note ἀμετακίνητοι εἶεν αὐτοῖς αἱ τιμαί [their honors should be unshaken].

Thus M, with the corrector having written ἐν [in] above μ, by which is signified τετιμέναι [having been honored], which suits neither the meter nor the sense, and with the scholium added: αἱ Ἐρινύες παρὰ τῶν χθονίων θεῶν τετιμημέναι [the Erinyes having been honored by the chthonic gods]. The true reading κλῦτε δὲ Γᾶ χθονίων τε τιμαί [hear, O Earth, and honors of the chthonic gods], H. L. Ahrens restored, about which I should have mentioned under the word Γἢ [Earth]. τιμή [honor] used of one who is worshipped is to be compared with the similar use of the word σέβας [reverence], which we discussed in its place. Hermann formerly in vain proposed κλῦτε δὲ τὰ χθονίων τιτηνά [hear the Titanic things of the chthonic gods], later κλῦτε δὲ τὰ χθονίων πρότιμα [hear the preeminent things of the chthonic gods]. Similarly Γἢ [Earth] and χθόνιοι θεοί [chthonic gods] are elsewhere joined: see under χθόνιος [chthonic].
